rounds.text: Supreme Power Equipment Ltd trades at a P/E of 25.4x [E1], yet the business demonstrates exceptional capital efficiency, delivering an ROE of 19.4% [E13] and an ROCE of 22.0% [E12] that substantially outperform sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Operational momentum is exceptional, backed by a rule-based screen score of 98 out of 100 [E54], three-year compounded profit growth of 24% [E16], and TTM sales growth reaching 46% [E15]. Growth visibility is exceptionally high, supported by an order book exceeding INR 565.80 crores [E77] and management guidance projecting full-year FY27 revenue between INR 300 crores and INR 350 crores [E64] on the path toward a combined peak revenue potential of INR 550 crores to INR 600 crores [E71]. Working capital management has improved significantly as debtor days dropped from 139 to 94.1 days [E50] and total working capital requirements compressed from 94.0 to 39.1 days [E51], ensuring robust cash conversion of 1.24x backed by Rs 26 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026 [E25, E26]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests a material valuation gap by estimating intrinsic value at Rs 408 per share against the current market price of Rs 251 [E36], leaving a margin of safety of 38.5% [E37]. Conceded: operating margins have compressed by 3 percentage points to 17% [E21] amid inflationary pressures on key raw materials like CRGO steel [E74], and free cash flow was negative at Rs -32 Cr in March 2026 [E27].

Supreme Power Equipment Ltd carries valuation and fundamental risks that are not fully supported by its headline growth figures. The stock trades at a premium P/E of 25.13x and EV/EBITDA of 15.56x, both exceeding sector benchmarks of 21.23x and 11.89x respectively [E6, E11]. Furthermore, despite reporting profits, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% and does not pay out any dividends [E4, E52]. Free cash flow for March 2026 was deeply negative at Rs -32 Cr [E27], and borrowings increased to Rs 57 Cr in September 2026 up from Rs 50 Cr a year earlier [E30]. Conceded: the company displays strong 3-year compounded sales and profit growth of 22% and 24% alongside a healthy order book [E14, E16, E77]. However, operating margins have compressed by 3 percentage points over the TTM and year-ago periods amid inflationary pressures and raw material price volatility [E21, E22, E75], while institutional shareholding has experienced a sharp contraction from foreign and domestic entities since December 2023 [E33, E34].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 25.13x and EV/EBITDA of 15.56x above sector benchmarks [E6, E11], offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], and experienced negative free cash flow of Rs -32 Cr in March 2026 [E27]. However, this premium valuation is fully justified by superior operational returns, including an ROE of 18.72% and ROCE of 20.73% that vastly outperform sector medians [E9, E10]. The modest rise in borrowings to Rs 57 Cr [E30] supports tangible growth, evidenced by a robust order book exceeding ₹565.80 crores [E77] and successful ramp-up of the Kannur facility [E70, E72]. Margin pressures from input costs [E75] are actively mitigated by price variation clauses covering 70% to 75% of the order book [E73]. Finally, concerns regarding institutional exits [E33, E34] are outweighed by positive institutional money flow [E35] and a high promoter stake of 57.16% [E32].

However, the bull's claim that price variation clauses mitigate input cost pressures [E73] ignores the reality that 25% to 30% of the order book remains entirely unprotected, directly driving a continuous multi-year operating margin compression down to 17% [E21, E23] and creating a vulnerable timing lag between rising input costs and price adjustments [E81]. Furthermore, dismissing the severe negative free cash flow of Rs -32 Cr [E27] and rising borrowings to Rs 57 Cr [E30] as mere support for growth overlooks the tangible financial strain, especially when paired with a thin current ratio buffer of 1.28x [E29]. Conceded: promoter holding is stable at 57.16% [E32]; nevertheless, this does not offset the massive desertion by sophisticated institutional capital, evidenced by foreign and domestic institutional holdings plummeting by 8.46 and 11.08 percentage points respectively since Dec 2023 [E33, E34]. Finally, the bull's valuation defense collapses because trading at a premium P/E of 25.13x and EV/EBITDA of 15.56x [E6, E11] with a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] is fundamentally misaligned with an explicitly flagged warning that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E53].

Conceded: 25% to 30% of the order book lacks price variation clauses [E73]. However, the bear overstates the margin impact because 70% to 75% of the book is protected [E73], and current order book strength sits at over ₹565.80 crores to drive upcoming execution [E77]. Conceded: free cash flow reached ₹-32 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27] and borrowings rose to ₹57 Cr [E30]. Yet operating cash flow remained robust at ₹26 Cr with a 1.24x conversion rate, fully backing profits with actual cash [E25, E26], while management specifically affirmed that cash flow from operations will turn positive in the second half [E83]. The institutional holding decrease [E33, E34] is directly counterbalanced by positive institutional money flow showing a recent holding increase [E35] alongside stable promoter backing at 57.16% [E32]. Finally, the premium valuation multiples [E6, E11] are fully justified by superior capital efficiency metrics like an 18.72% ROE and 20.73% ROCE beating sector benchmarks [E9, E10], complemented by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹408 providing a 38.5% margin of safety [E36, E37].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached ₹26 Cr with a 1.24x conversion rate [E25, E26], but this did not prevent free cash flow from plunging to a heavy deficit of ₹-32 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27]. Conceded: 70% to 75% of the order book carries price variation protection [E73], yet management explicitly warns that timing differences between input cost spikes in materials like CRGO steel and subsequent price adjustments continue to compress margins [E74, E81]. Operating margins have demonstrably eroded by 3 percentage points down to 17% [E21, E22], accompanied by a yearly trend that reads as steadily decreasing over four years [E23]. While management projects cash flow to turn positive in the second half [E83], borrowings have already climbed to ₹57 Cr [E30] and the company faces pressure requiring higher working capital limits from banks [E79]. Furthermore, dismissing the steep institutional exodus—where foreign and domestic holdings collapsed from 9.21% and 11.31% down to 0.75% and 0.23% respectively [E33, E34]—cannot be offset by a minor short-term uptick [E35], especially when the stock carries high annualised volatility of 71.2% and a brutal historical drawdown of -74.2% [E44, E45].
